simple.meaning: הָזָה (hâzâh) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to dream.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 1 time in Isaiah, beginning at Isaiah 56:10. Its meaning becomes clearer as the uses are compared.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to הָזָה (H1957) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: הָזָה (hâzâh) / H1957 is traced through Isaiah 56:10 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.full: H1957. hazah [ הָזָה ] verb dream, rave (Arabic talk deliriously , Syriac , in Lexicons, id. , compare also Vrss; see especially Bo Hieroz. ii. 56; ed. Rosenm. vol. i. 782 ). — only Qal Participle active plural הֹזִים Isa 56:10 ה ׳לִנְבֹּ֑חַ שֹׁכְּבִים יוּכְלוּ לֹא of dogs, metaphor of false prophets.
